newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh to set aside portion of IPOs for expats.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh to set aside portion of IPOs for expats.

text.p: Expatriate Bangladeshis will soon be able to purchase stock under a new system reserving five percent of each initial public offering (IPO) for them, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) chief said on Tuesday.
"We have already prepared the documents and now it is up to the central bank to examine technical details and grant final approval," SEC Chairman Harunur Rashid told Reuters.
"The quota system is expected to come into force next month," he said. "We are doing the job seriously as Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina desires it to be done quickly."
Hasina on Sunday directed the SEC, the market watchdog, to implement a quota system soon.

At a meeting with Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) officials on Monday, Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria said the government would allow Bangladeshi citizens living overseas to invest in the primary capital market.

This will fulfil a promise by the finance minister in his budget speech in July that Bangladesh expatriates, who remit home more than $1 billion annually, would be given a chance to invest in their own country.
"The SEC initiative has been driven by that promise," one official said.

Kibria said: "At present expatriates have no opportunity to invest directly in primary shares. But they are contributing to our economy significantly. So the government has decided to make provisions for them to directly participate in the primary market."
Under rules prepared by the SEC, expatriates can invest either directly or through nominees.
Currently 70 percent of the shares in each IPO are reserved for sale to locals and the rest set aside for foreign investors.
After the introduction of the five percent quota for expatriates, the percentage of shares reserved for investors in Bangladesh will drop to 65 percent.

To make it easier for expatriate investors, authorities are planning to extend the time limit for applications to purchase IPO shares, SEC sources said. The time period currently lasts between seven and 10 days.
